subject: MAP close sprint — seed org, short-lived API keys, IP allowlist & VPC peering window
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia@healthsync.io>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: MAP close cadence + network/keys questions

Hi Priya + Ben,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday — the MAP looks promising and we want to lock the final steps so our security and infra teams can greenlight the POC. A couple of asks from our side to close the loop: 

- Org seed: will Redwood create an org with a test tenant that we can join, or do you want us to create a named org and invite Redwood?
- API keys: we prefer short-lived keys for the trial (30m–4hr TTL) and a clear rotation process. Can Redwood issue ephemeral keys by default?
- IP allowlist: we'll need the exact egress IP ranges to add to our firewall (staging and prod ranges separately if you can).
- VPC peering: preferred peering window this month is Jul 27–29. Any blackout windows we should avoid?

I attached our security questionnaire (first pass). Can you confirm a final close date so procurement can schedule a DocuSign for the PO?

Appreciate it —
Olivia

--
Olivia Chen
Head of Integrations, HealthSync
olivia@healthsync.io
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@healthsync.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP close cadence + network/keys questions

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise runbook we can follow to clinch the MAP and get your POC env live within the Jul 27–29 peering window if that still works for you.

1) Org seed (T+0)
- We will create a temporary org in the Redwood Private control plane and add 2 HealthSync admins you nominate. If you'd rather create the org and invite us, say the word; both work.
- Deliverable: org_id and admin invite by EOD Jul 23.

2) API keys (T+1)
- We will issue a short-lived API key flow: initial provisioning key (4 hr TTL) and ephemeral session keys (30 min TTL) for test runners. Keys auto-rotate; we provide an example script for rotation.
- Deliverable: sample rotation script + initial provisioning key by Jul 24.

3) IP allowlist (T+1)
- Ben to provide the staging egress CIDR block and a separate prod-ish block we use for Dedicated. If you need static NAT, we can reserve a single IP for the peering test.
- Deliverable: ip_ranges.csv and allowlist template by Jul 23.

4) VPC peering (window Jul 27–29)
- Preferred approach: one-time peering for the POC VPC (staging). We'll coordinate the exact window with your infra lead; avoid Jul 28 12:00–14:00 PST due to maintenance.
- Deliverable: peering request + connection test results by Jul 28 morning.

5) Security checklist + procurement (T+2)
- We will review the attached questionnaire and highlight anything that requires evidence (SOC 2 report, API logs retention settings, KMS integration notes).
- If procurement needs a PO/DocuSign, we can start the paperwork once org_id is issued.

Next steps: Ben — can you attach the CIDR blocks and a quick network runbook? Jordan/Neha — please confirm the ephemeral key TTLs and any ops steps for rotation so I can include them in the MAP. Olivia — can you confirm who your infra contact is for the peering setup?

Thanks,
Priya

--
Priya Natarajan

Quick infra notes from my side:

- Ephemeral keys: provisioning key TTL = 4h; session keys = 30m; all keys will be listed in the audit log and expire server-side (no client revocation needed).
- Org seed: we can pre-populate roles (admin, engineer, readonly) and a sandbox project for HealthSync. We will document the minimal IAM mapping you should use.
- Logs & retention: default request logs for the POC are retained for 30 days; we can extend if needed (extra cost).

I'll add a one-page ops playbook that shows how to rotate keys automatically using our example script (bash + curl).

-Neha
